name: Danau
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Wikipedia. 2023-2025. 'Danau language' (phonology section citing Aung Si 2014:1108, Nu Nu Thein 2005, Luce 1965, Sidwell 2015).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Secondary. Says /ə/ and /n̩/ 'are found only in the first (weak) syllable of sesquisyllabic words'; tonal language, 3 (or 4) tones, tone sandhi. No sentence about stress.

sources.citation: Htanaw Sar project (Jenny, Han Tin, Weymuth, Herdeg). 2023. 'Htanaw alphabet' and 'Htanaw resources' pages, htanawsar.org / sites.google.com/view/htanawsar.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Alphabet page: 'Htanaw distinguishes three lexical tones: low/low-falling, mid/mid-falling, and high/high-rising'; inherent vowel 'pronounced ɐ in closed syllables, ə in open syllables (presyllables)'; tone sandhi. No statement on stress. Resources page is the bibliography used for the list of works to obtain and supplied the public link to the Nu Nu Thein dissertation.

sources.citation: Jenny, Mathias, Han Tin, Rachel Weymuth, Alexandra Herdeg & Ampika Rattanapitak. 2022. Writing Htanaw in Burmese script: challenges in devising an orthography. Slides, ICAAL 10, 1-2 Dec 2022 (20 pp.).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology slide gives full syllables CV, CVC, CCV, CCVC; presyllables Cə, N̩; rhymes V, VV, VC(h, ʔ, ɴ) + tone; 14 vowels + 5 diphthongs; onsets with [±implosive], [±aspirate]; three lexical tones. Nothing on stress ('accent' occurs only in the phrase 'written with a Burmese accent').

sources.citation: Jenny, Mathias, Rachel Weymuth, Alexandra Herdeg & Han Tin. 2022. Htanaw alphabetization and documentation (dataset v1.0). SWISSUbase, DOI 10.48656/vxhj-mn25.
sources.note: Recordings, transcripts and metadata (one zip); overview page has no phonological description.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1, languoid dana1252 (refs: Si 2015; Nu Nu Thein 2005; Sidwell 2015 classification).
sources.note: Lists only the two descriptive refs already in the target record; no phonology content.

sources.citation: Si, Aung. 2014. Documentation of Danau, an endangered language of Myanmar (Burma). ELAR deposit 0321, hdl 2196/00-0000-0000-0002-A17B-C.
sources.note: Deposit page read: audio, transcriptions, 'preliminary analysis of the phonetics, phonology and grammar of Danau'; language 'exhibits a tonal system'. Grammar elicitation PDFs (Grammar 1-3) require ELAR login (handle redirects to a Preservica sign-up page). No stress statement on the open pages.

sources.citation: Nu Nu Thein (မနုနုသိန်း). 2005. ထနော့ဘာသာစကားလေ့လာချက် [Study of the Htanaw language]. PhD dissertation, Yangon University. 210 pp. (Burmese).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Chapter 1 'sound system' (pp. 1-54 = PDF 32-85) has sections on consonants, vowels, syllable system (1.4, pp. 35-43: syllable types OVO/OVC/CVO/CVC, clusters, word-length counts 1-4 syllables, presyllables written pə-, kə-, tă-), tone system (1.5, pp. 44-51: Htanaw is a tone language with three tones, creaky /ˊ/, level /-/, heavy-falling /ˋ/; cites Luce 1965:99-100 for a 4-tone analysis) and vowel length (1.6, pp. 52-54). Read pages 1-3 and 35-54 as page images (scan; text layer is garbage, no Burmese tesseract data on the box). No mention of word stress anywhere in these sections.

sources.citation: Si, Aung. 2015 [2014]. Danau. In M. Jenny & P. Sidwell (eds), The Handbook of Austroasiatic Languages, vol. 2, 1104-1141. Leiden: Brill.
